reference.criterion: Automation reduces transportation accidents to a very low societal burden, not just a modest statistical improvement.
reference.rationale: Transport injury and death remained a major global burden around the target date. WHO’s 2021 estimate of 1.19 million annual road deaths, only modestly below 2010, contradicts the very-few-accidents scenario. Individual safer systems do not establish the whole-system outcome.

evidence.title: WHO: Global road safety progress remains insufficient
evidence.note: 2021 global annual road deaths 1.19 million; about 5% below 2010. These are observed-year figures, not invented 2026 counts.. 2021 global annual road deaths 1.19 million; about 5% below 2010. These are observed-year figures, not invented 2026 counts.

broader.rationale: Improvement is real but uneven and far weaker than the original near-elimination scenario.
